## Hello

I am a Master of Data Science student at the University of British Columbia, here on
a **CAD $10,000 MDS Scholarship**. I came from computer science at National Tsing
Hua University in Taiwan, where I spent four years as a software engineer working at
the hardest end of machine learning infrastructure: making very large models run on
GPU clusters, and teaching other students how to do it.

That work put me on the floor at the world's top supercomputing competitions. My
teams took **1st place at the 2023 APAC HPC-AI Competition in Australia**, **2nd at ISC High
Performance 2024** in Germany, and **3rd at SC24** in America — three of the most
competitive HPC-AI events in the world, where fewer than twenty teams are selected
from a global applicant pool to compete in person. Along the way we made BLOOM
inference 11.4× faster, a CFD solver 18.5× faster, and a 70B-parameter chatbot serve
3× the throughput.

Then I spent a summer as a **Data Scientist at IBM**, watching models meet the real
world, and it reframed everything. My understanding of AI was almost entirely
system-side: throughput, kernels, parallelism, deployment. The modelling half — the
part that decides whether a result is worth deploying at all — I had only ever
picked up in passing. **MDS is me completing that half deliberately.**

What I am building toward is a full-stack ML engineer: someone who can take a
problem through model development, training, and evaluation *and* through the
acceleration, deployment, and pipeline work that gets it into production — because
those are usually the same problem, and they are rarely the same person.

I am looking for **machine learning engineer**, **data scientist**, and **software
engineering** roles. More on the [about page](about.qmd), my work is on
[projects](projects.qmd), and I write about the program on the [blog](blog.qmd).
